issue_context.title: IsStandAlone is set to late after PR #21200

## Bug report
### Describe the bug
Here is a clear and concise description of what the problem is:

Setting is hidden because of wrong status of requirement [IsStandAlone](https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/blob/master/system/settings/settings.xml#L2503)
<!--- Provide a more detailed introduction to the issue itself, and why you consider it to be a bug -->

<!--- Put your text below this line -->



## Expected Behavior
Here is a clear and concise description of what was expected to happen:
<!--- Tell us what should happen -->
<!--- Put your text below this line -->
[IsStandAlone](https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/blob/master/xbmc/Application.h#L271) need to be initialized before SettingsConditions get initialized.


## Actual Behavior
<!--- Tell us what happens instead -->
<!--- Put your text below this line -->
[m_bStandalone](https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/blob/master/xbmc/Application.cpp#L335) is set to late.


## Possible Fix
<!--- Not obligatory, but suggest a fix or reason for the bug -->

<!--- Provide a link to a live example, or an unambiguous set of steps to -->

comments:
I am sure much more issues will pop up in future like https://github.com/xbmc/xbmc/issues/21240.
The CLog class is already destroyed and get accessed by CFDEventMonitor afterwards on thread stop.

The start/create/init/stop/unregister/destroy chains are now completely messed up.

Yes, and those issues need to be fixed to finally get a well defined stop/uninit/destroy chain. Before it all was a mess and worked only, because the logging component was never destroyed or to be more precise, being a global static variable it was destroyed at a random point in time while the application exited.

Regarding IsStandAlone: Another design flaw that needs to be fixed. Application depends on settings and settings depends on Application (circular dependency).

`XBMC_GLOBAL_REF(CFDEventMonitor, g_fdEventMonitor);`

 Yep, another static global instance, which gets destroyed at a random point in time when Kodi exits. Fix is to get rid of it by constructing/destructing it in a controllable manner.
Yes, it's a problem and the structure about construction and destruction needs to be fixed to avoid randomly happen segment faults. But this will result in some work... ☹️

review_comments: You don't seem to check for nullptr anywhere that `GetAppParams` is called. I believe it should always be available, however, do you think we should add a nullptr check here and throw or log if it is?

App params is supposed to be available as the very first "service" and calling it when it is not yet available is a logical error in the application, so we should throw a logic_error. Will change this.
